headline: UK Graduate Visa 2026: A Canadian Applicant's Guide
metaDescription: Canadians who graduated from a UK university: Graduate visa rules for 2026, application fees and the health surcharge, work rights, and what changes in 2027.

sections.content:
The Graduate visa lets international students — including Canadians who studied in the UK — stay and work, or look for work, without needing a sponsoring employer. It is one of the most flexible routes in the UK immigration system: there is no job offer requirement, no salary threshold, no maintenance funds requirement and no English test. Almost any job is allowed, including self-employment and freelance work, with the single exception of professional sport.

Timing matters more than ever. Applications made on or before 31 December 2026 get two years of stay, or three years for PhD graduates. From 1 January 2027, the standard grant drops to 18 months, while PhD graduates keep three years. If you are finishing your UK degree in 2026, the date of your application decides which set of rules you fall under.
sections.title: What the Graduate Route Gives You

sections.content:
You must apply online from inside the UK, before your Student visa expires — you cannot apply for the Graduate visa from abroad, so do not fly home to Canada before you have applied. Your university must have reported your successful course completion to the Home Office before you apply, so check with your institution's immigration team rather than assuming the paperwork is done. Only students who completed an eligible UK degree qualify.

Once granted, you are free to work at any skill level while you look for longer-term sponsorship. But plan ahead: the Graduate visa cannot be extended, and time spent on it does not count toward settlement under the Skilled Worker route — though it may count toward the ten-year long residence route. Many Canadian graduates use the time to secure a sponsored Skilled Worker role.
sections.title: Who Can Apply

sections.content:
The application fee is around £937 — note that some older sources still cite £822, so check the current figure on gov.uk before you apply, as fees are updated periodically. On top of that, you pay the Immigration Health Surcharge upfront for the full grant: £1,035 per year, which works out at roughly £2,070 for a two-year visa. The surcharge gives you access to the NHS on broadly the same basis as residents.

Budget for the total before you start the application, because both payments are due when you apply and are generally non-refundable. There is no maintenance requirement — you do not need to show savings — but the upfront cost is real, so factor it into your post-graduation plans alongside rent and living costs in the UK.
sections.title: Fees and the Immigration Health Surcharge

sections.content:
Work rights are deliberately broad. You can take any job at any skill level, switch employers freely, and work as self-employed or freelance. That flexibility is the route's main selling point: it buys you up to two years to build UK experience, grow a professional network and find an employer willing to sponsor you under the Skilled Worker route.

The only notable exclusion is professional sport, including coaching — you cannot work as a professional sportsperson on this visa. Everything else, from graduate schemes to part-time work to running your own business, is permitted. Your employer needs no sponsor licence and faces no extra paperwork, which removes a real barrier when job hunting.
sections.title: Working on the Graduate Visa

sections.content:
The hard limits: the visa cannot be extended, and time on it does not count toward Skilled Worker settlement — it can, however, count toward the ten-year long residence route. You also cannot travel outside the UK while your application is pending; leaving the Common Travel Area withdraws the application automatically, so stay put until you get a decision, which typically takes around eight weeks.

Dependants need attention too. A new dependant rule for UK-born babies took effect on 3 August 2026, and partners can only join in limited circumstances — the Graduate route is primarily for the graduate themselves. If your long-term plan is settlement, use the Graduate period strategically: it is a bridge to sponsored work, not a destination.
